text: Scan local git repositories including full history using git log -p under the hood
quote: The `git` command lets you scan local git repos. Under the hood, gitleaks uses the `git log -p` command to scan patches.

text: Scan directories and individual files for secrets via the dir command
quote: The `dir` (aliases include `files`, `directory`) command lets you scan directories and files. Example: `gitleaks dir -v path_to_directory_or_file`.

text: Stream arbitrary data into gitleaks via stdin for scanning non-file sources
quote: You can also stream data to gitleaks with the `stdin` command. Example: `cat some_file | gitleaks -v stdin`

text: Run gitleaks as a pre-commit git hook to block secrets before they're committed
quote: You can run Gitleaks as a pre-commit hook by copying the example `pre-commit.py` script into your `.git/hooks/` directory.

text: Pre-commit hook fails the commit and reports detected hardcoded secrets
quote:
➜ git commit -m "this commit contains a secret"
Detect hardcoded secrets.................................................Failed

text: Write custom secret-detection rules using gitleaks' own configuration format
quote: Gitleaks offers a configuration format you can follow to write your own secret detection rules

text: Composite rules combine a primary rule with required auxiliary rules for more precise detection
quote: In v8.28.0 Gitleaks introduced composite rules, which are made up of a single "primary" rule and one or more auxiliary or `required` rules.

text: Baseline a set of known findings so future scans only report new secrets
quote: When using a baseline, gitleaks will ignore any old findings that are present in the baseline.

text: Findings output (findings.json) can be filtered to only new issues via --baseline-path
quote: After running the detect command with the --baseline-path parameter, report output (findings.json) will only contain new issues.

text: Install gitleaks via Homebrew, Docker, or Go
quote: Gitleaks can be installed using Homebrew, Docker, or Go.

text: GitHub Action alerts you as soon as secrets are leaked in your workflows
quote: Enable **Gitleaks-Action** in your GitHub workflows to be alerted when secrets are leaked as soon as they happen.

text: gitleaks-action posts PR comments via the GitHub API when secrets are found
quote: **gitleaks-action** uses this token to call [a GitHub API](https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v18#pulls-create-review-comment) to comment on PRs.

text: Configure a list of GitHub accounts to be emailed/alerted when a leak is detected
quote: A list of GitHub accounts that should be alerted when gitleaks-action detects a leak. An email will be sent by GitHub to the user

text: Display a 'protected by gitleaks' badge in your project readme
quote: Enable this gitleaks-action and copy to your readme.

text: Automatically scan all team pull requests and commits, or trigger on-demand scans
quote: You can use it to automatically run a gitleaks scan on all your team's pull requests and commits, or run on-demand scans.

text: Set a custom config path via GITLEAKS_CONFIG or auto-detect a gitleaks.toml at repo root
quote: You can use `GITLEAKS_CONFIG` to explicitly set a config path _or_ create a `gitleaks.toml` at the root of the repo which will be automatically detected and used by **gitleaks-action**.

text: Detects hardcoded secrets like passwords, API keys, and tokens across git, files, and stdin input
quote: Gitleaks is a tool for detecting secrets like passwords, API keys, and tokens in git repos, files, and whatever else you wanna throw at it via stdin.

text: Supports three scanning modes: git, dir, and stdin
quote: There are three scanning modes: git, dir, and stdin.
